segments.title: Chương 142: Mỗi ngày vẽ ra viễn cảnh và khích lệ nhân viên
segments.content:
Chapter 145: Motivating Employees with Pie-in-the-Sky Promises Daily (Bonus Chapter for Alliance Leader Badaolege)

Senior Brother Min, who was secretly nursing a broken heart, had already recovered his spirits. He even asked with great interest, "Chen Guiliang, are you going to the Two Sessions Forum?"

"What Two Sessions Forum?" Chen Guiliang asked, puzzled.

Min Wenyu explained, "Every year during the Two Sessions, they invite entrepreneurs who have just attended to come to Peking University for an MBA forum. This year's theme is 'Brand China: From Made in China to Created in China'."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Who's participating this year?"

Min Wenyu said, "I saw on the promotional poster that the bosses of Himin Solar and Sanquan Foods will be there. Also, the director of CCTV's advertising department, and some director from a food engineering technology center."

"No internet companies?" Chen Guiliang asked.

"No, all traditional industries," Min Wenyu said.

"Then I'm not going," Chen Guiliang said.

This kind of forum was just a chance to listen to entrepreneurs brag, and he'd probably get a stomach full of chicken soup for the soul.

There wouldn't be any real substance.

If it were related to the internet, Chen Guiliang might have gone to expand his network.

But he would pass on traditional industries.

Senior Brother Min, however, was very enthusiastic and rode his bicycle straight to the lecture hall. The forum was jointly organized by the Peking University MBA Association and CCTV's advertising department. Senior Brother Min wanted to go and make his face known, hoping it might lead to an internship at CCTV in the future.

"Are you going too?" Chen Guiliang asked, seeing Jiang Junlai running outside.

Jiang Junlai said, "I'm going to another presentation."

With the Two Sessions underway, Peking University had invited quite a few delegates, and various forums and presentations were popping up one after another.

After Senior Brother Min and Jiang Junlai left, Chen Guiliang sat in front of his computer, opened a portal website, and began to read the government report. Reading this was far more useful than attending those school events.

Having been reborn and combining it with the experiences of his past life, Chen Guiliang could see so, so much more when reading the report this time!

First and foremost was Shanghai real estate. Less than a month after the Two Sessions ended, the hammer would come down hard. Things like a certain property's price plummeting by 42% or owners of 300 units in another property collectively pulling out of their purchases would be common.

Those who speculated on property with loans would meet a tragic end this year.

Of course, it was also a good opportunity for the wealthy to buy at the bottom, like the vast cohort of coal bosses. This year would see a large-scale, mandatory shutdown of small coal mines. Many coal bosses would be left with nothing but money, perfect for them to wave around their cash and buy up property at low prices.

In the blink of an eye, it was Friday, and Peng Fei arrived in Beijing ahead of schedule.

He had already found out what Chen Guiliang did through an internet search, but he was still surprised to see the sheet music. "CEO Chen wrote this song?"

"You could say that," Chen Guiliang said.

Peng Fei asked, "Are there any specific requirements for the arrangement?"

Chen Guiliang knew nothing about that, so he could only say, "I hope you can carefully ponder the lyrics and make the arrangement fit their mood."

"Understood." Peng Fei took the music and lyrics and left. He still had to find friends to rent equipment from.

That afternoon, Peng Fei called again. "CEO Chen, someone wants to buy your song."

"Who is it?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Peng Fei said, "Li Jian from Shui Mu Nian Hua. Of course, he's gone solo now. The song is called 'When the Wind Blows,' and he wants to include it on his next solo album."

Chen Guiliang asked, "How does he know about this song?"

Peng Fei explained, "I've arranged the string sections for his songs before, and we've kept in touch ever since. I don't have many friends in Beijing, so this time I asked him for help borrowing some equipment. He happened to be free and even helped me with ideas for the arrangement. He fell for your song at first sight. The price is negotiable."

Chen Guiliang said, "Please tell him for me that this is Xiaonei.com's theme song and it will be released online this year. If he wants to include it in his album, I don't want a single cent; he can have the license to sing it for free. But he must mention Xiaonei.com during the recording."

"Okay, I'll pass that on to him." Peng Fei hung up.

Chen Guiliang put down his phone and, as he did daily, logged into 5Q Campus Network to observe the enemy.

This time, he was greeted by a line of red text on the homepage: "Warmly celebrating 5Q Campus Network's registered users surpassing the 100,000 mark."

Having money was just that domineering. With their frenzied promotion, they had actually broken 100,000 users so quickly. This was especially true of their on-the-ground promotions in dorms, where they watched students register and then gave them small gifts.

However, registering was one thing, and actually using it was another.

User activity on 5Q Campus Network seemed to be a problem.

After all, Chen Guiliang had already seized the first-mover advantage. One step ahead, always ahead.

Chen Guiliang sent a text to his Fudan classmate, Milan: "At Fudan, do more people use Xiaonei.com or 5Q Campus Network?"

Milan replied, "A lot of students use both sites. But from the few friends I know, they only log into 5Q Campus Network when they want to write a journal entry or upload a photo album. For interaction between classmates, they still mainly use Xiaonei.com."

This situation was very common, as there were too many similar websites.

For example, those who enjoyed blogging would, after finishing an article, post it on multiple blog sites, as well as on Xiaonei.com and 5Q Campus Network. They went through all this trouble mainly to get more people to see it.

Right now, Xiaonei.com had nearly 500,000 registered users, while 5Q Campus Network had just surpassed 100,000.

There was still a huge gap in the market.

It needed a breakout moment to break through its circle.

The role of "Happy Farm" was more to increase user stickiness.

"When the Wind Blows" was what would truly be used to break out.

The Mandopop scene was a battle of gods these days, but the gods had their own track, and online songs had theirs. "When the Wind Blows" was precisely targeted at the student population.

Meanwhile, Ao Yanchen was still on the phone.

"Hello, this is ByteDance's Xiaonei.com. I saw that your company's product has ads placed on Sohu... It's okay if you haven't heard of us. Xiaonei.com is the number one campus social networking site, using a real-name registration system. All our users are high-quality university students..."

"You can come and take a look at our website. The homepage ad is currently placed by Tencent... We only offer three ad slots on the entire site, and every single one can be seen by users... You don't need to worry about the ad's effectiveness. Even QQ, which just released its new email service, chose to advertise on Xiaonei.com. You can imagine how effective we are..."

"Mhm, okay, okay, your company can take your time to discuss it..."

Ao Yanchen made one call after another. After twenty or thirty calls, she rubbed her face and leaned back exhaustedly in her chair.

Seeing Chen Guiliang walk over, Senior Sister Ao complained, "You have to give me a raise!"

"Okay," Chen Guiliang said, but didn't specify when.

Ao Yanchen and Dong Qianqiu still had a lot of faith in Chen Guiliang.

Although they complained about the capitalist, they knew Chen Guiliang was a man with a conscience.

Chen Guiliang had registered Game Science by himself; he had even submitted the application before classes officially started. This company was his sole proprietorship.

Guo Feng had joined ByteDance, receiving 10% equity at the time of registration.

During this period, Game Science had been constantly funneling blood into ByteDance, which was equivalent to Chen Guiliang continuously pouring his own money into the company. Under normal circumstances, Guo Feng's 10% equity would have long been diluted to nothing.

However, Chen Guiliang had never mentioned altering the equity structure, and Guo Feng's 10% had remained undiluted.

This made Guo Feng feel a bit embarrassed, and he even took the initiative to suggest reducing his equity.

As for the stock options for Ao Yanchen and Dong Qianqiu, those would typically be determined when they received investment. Even if Chen Guiliang didn't want to give them out, the investors would demand an option pool be set up, usually around 10-15%.

"CEO Chen, when do you think real venture capital will come?" Ao Yanchen asked with anticipation.

Due to all the trouble with the previous MSN deal, Ao Yanchen didn't consider it real VC.

Chen Guiliang said, "We're benchmarking ourselves against Facebook. The more attention Facebook gets in the US, the sooner VCs will come looking for us, and our valuation will also be higher."

Ao Yanchen daydreamed, "If I become a millionaire, I'll buy a house in Beijing. When my parents retire, I'll bring them over to enjoy their lives too."

"You'd be satisfied with just being a millionaire?" Chen Guiliang chuckled.

Ao Yanchen laughed too, then pulled herself together. "Time to make calls and get ads!"

Chen Guiliang was just there to give them a shot of adrenaline. After he was done, he immediately left to continue chatting with other employees.

Over on Facebook's side, they were currently in talks with VCs. In just over a month, they would complete their Series A funding, with a post-money valuation of $100 million!

By that time, VCs should start taking notice of Xiaonei.com.

"Old Chen, Xiaonei.com's user growth is too fast. We need to upgrade the servers and bandwidth again," Guo Feng said to Chen Guiliang. "After the upgrade, Xiaonei.com's monthly operating costs might exceed 100,000 RMB, and that's not including employee salaries. If that song of yours really blows up and brings in a huge number of users in a short time, we'll have to consider upgrading even sooner. Monthly operating costs might be heading towards 150,000 RMB."

Chen Guiliang said, "It's fine. Three Kingdoms Kill can still provide funding, and Xiaonei.com is already taking ads. We've also finalized things with the online payment services. Xiaonei.com will launch a top-up function next month. We can earn a little something by selling background themes and letter papers."

Guo Feng said, a bit sheepishly, "I was talking about my 10% equity. You keep pouring money in, should we lower mine a bit more?"

"What do you think is a suitable amount?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Guo Feng analyzed rationally, "For the future stability of the company, it's best to reserve a 15% option pool. I can reduce my stake to 8% now and not take any options. For the first round of investment, we'll probably give 10-15% to the investors. By then, I'll still have over 7% equity."

Chen Guiliang thought about it carefully. "That works. If you ever feel you're getting a raw deal, I can give you some options at my discretion."

"It's settled then." Guo Feng smiled, finally feeling at ease.

Chen Guiliang continued to patrol his territory, making small talk with the employees and casually asking about their well-being and discussing work.

After touring ByteDance, he went next door to Game Science.

When Xu Fengyin saw him coming, she quickly buried her head in her drawing. Saying even a single word would feel awkward.

Fortunately, Chen Guiliang never mentioned that comic book.

"CEO Chen, the boss's wife is here!" an employee called out.

Chen Guiliang turned and left. Xu Fengyin finally breathed a sigh of relief.

The young woman at the next workstation leaned over to gossip with her. "Have you seen the boss's wife?"

Xu Fengyin was puzzled. "The boss is married?"

"His girlfriend. She's incredibly beautiful," the young woman said.

Xu Fengyin couldn't help but turn her head to look, seeing a man and a woman standing at the doorway. The scene gave her a special feeling, making her want to turn it into a comic panel.

(End of this chapter)
